label: Bible Study
prompt: For sin shall not have _____ over you: for ye are not under the law, but under grace.
verse: For sin shall not have dominion over you: for ye are not under the law, but under grace.
note: Sin has lost its hold — believers live under grace, not under its rule.

label: Warm-Up Word
prompt: Finally, brethren, whatsoever things are _____, whatsoever things are honest, whatsoever things are just, whatsoever things are pure, whatsoever things are lovely, whatsoever things are of good report; if there be any virtue, and if there be any praise, think on these things.
verse: Finally, brethren, whatsoever things are true, whatsoever things are honest, whatsoever things are just, whatsoever things are pure, whatsoever things are lovely, whatsoever things are of good report; if there be any virtue, and if there be any praise, think on these things.
note: Paul's mental diet plan: think on whatsoever is true, honest, just, pure, lovely, and of good report.

label: Sunday School
prompt: Behold also the ships, which though they be so great, and are driven of fierce winds, yet are they turned about with a very small _____, whithersoever the governor listeth.
verse: Behold also the ships, which though they be so great, and are driven of fierce winds, yet are they turned about with a very small helm, whithersoever the governor listeth.
note: Same lesson at sea: great ships driven by fierce winds still turn by a very small helm.

label: Deep Water
prompt: By the rivers of Babylon, there we sat down, yea, we _____, when we remembered Zion.
verse: By the rivers of Babylon, there we sat down, yea, we wept, when we remembered Zion.
note: The exiles' lament in Babylon — Jerusalem's songs were too painful to sing in a foreign land.

label: Don't Play With Me
prompt: And the _____ was so sharp between them, that they departed asunder one from the other: and so Barnabas took Mark, and sailed unto Cyprus;
verse: And the contention was so sharp between them, that they departed asunder one from the other: and so Barnabas took Mark, and sailed unto Cyprus;
note: Paul and Barnabas split over John Mark — a 'contention' so sharp they sailed separate ways.
